brief.situation: 07:05 on a surgical unit. You are the day RN taking report from Rob, the night nurse, after a hard night. When you ask to do the bedside handover and double-check Mr. Lee's patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) pump together, Rob snaps that you 'always make day shift into an inspection' and wants to give a quick verbal report at the station and go home. Work out what is going on, keep the safety step, and deal with the conflict constructively.
handover: Your professional code asks for respect and civility with colleagues and makes you accountable for your own practice; bullying is never tolerated.
Unit policy: high-alert infusions such as PCA pumps are checked by both nurses at the bedside at handover; conflicts that affect patient care go to the charge nurse.
howItWorks: Choose what to ask or say. Each exchange takes a few minutes of the conversation; Rob answers at once, and the next choice waits for the exchange to finish.
The screen shows Rob, how hard he is pushing, your working relationship, what you know so far, and your note.
When the conversation ends you write your note and explain your reasoning.

reflection.question: For your note: what the conflict and the safety issue were, what you did and why, and how you kept the working relationship.

parts.label: The problem
parts.criteria: Separates the conflict (fatigue and a feeling of being judged) from the safety step that cannot be dropped (a two-nurse check of a reprogrammed PCA) and from a false record.
parts.modelAnswer: Rob's exhausted and feels judged, but the reprogrammed PCA still needs a two-nurse check, and I can't sign for a check that didn't happen.

parts.label: Ask, then act
parts.criteria: Asks about his night and the comment before answering; offers a fast, respectful way to do the check; declines to co-sign falsely.
parts.modelAnswer: I asked about his night and what was behind the comment, then offered to do the pump together in five minutes and declined to co-sign.

parts.label: The relationship and the channel
parts.criteria: Acknowledges his experience; takes the workload and feedback issue to the charge nurse, not threats or a public post; writes a factual note.
parts.modelAnswer: I acknowledged it was a rough night and that public write-ups hurt, took the bigger issue to the charge nurse, and documented the check.

scoring.modelReasoning: Constructive conflict management separates the person and the problem: Rob is exhausted and feels judged, and the safety step still has to happen. Ask about his night and the comment, acknowledge his experience, then keep the bedside double-check of the reprogrammed PCA by making it quick and shared. Decline to co-sign a check not done. Take the workload and feedback issue to the charge nurse (the documented channel), not threats or a public post, and document the check. Face-to-face handover with time for questions is the standard because poor hand-offs lead to sentinel events.
